subject: Solving Lotka-Volterra equations using the ODE solver (range restrictions on the sampler?)

messages.author: 4d17bc398c8d91b8
messages.subject: Solving Lotka-Volterra equations using the ODE solver (range restrictions on the sampler?)
parts:
Hi all,

I have implemented a simple Lotka-Volterra type equation as a function in stan as follows:
-----
functions {
      real[] lv(real t,
                 real[] y,
                 real[] theta,
                 real[] x_r,
                 int[] x_i) {
        real alpha_ab;  
        real beta_ab;
        real alpha_na;
        real beta_na;
        real dydt[2];
        
        alpha_ab<-theta[1];
        beta_ab<-theta[2];
        alpha_na<-theta[3];
        beta_na<-theta[4];

        dydt[1] <- alpha_ab*y[2]-beta_ab*y[1];
        dydt[2] <- y[2]*(alpha_na-beta_na*y[1]);
        return dydt;
} }
----
(full code is  attached)
This works great for generating synthetic data with a known starting set of variables. However, when trying to estimate the thetas using those synthetic data,
the sampler quickly runs into problems. When using print to debug, it seems as if integrate_ode stalls for v.large/small parameter values. In the last run, the sampler picked values 
of 

theta<-c(1.00422e+07,9.17141e-22,2.23805e+30,1.31472e-32)
y0<-c(7.19909,531.881)

,just before the call to integrate_ode, and then nothing happened. Feeding these parameter values to the synthetic data generator also results in a stalled stan. 
I suspect that the problem is the combination of large and small values, and numerical issues related to that. What would be the best way of solving this issue? Putting a hard range limit on the thetas and y0?  checking for reasonable parameter values in an iff statement before the integration call? Some other way of informing the sampler that extreme values will be a problem? 

Best regards,
Gustaf

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Solving Lotka-Volterra equations using the ODE solver (range restrictions on the sampler?)
parts:
Hi Gustaf and Markus,

Sorry -- I completely missed the first message.

In Stan, we currently have a non-stiff solver. (Boost's 5th order Runga Kutta.) When parameter values are very large or very small, we're finding that even systems that are usually non-stiff may get into stiff regions.

We are currently working to get a stiff solver into Stan, but until that happens, one workaround is to put a reject statement within the system function when the parameters are very large / small. Although this puts a discontinuity in the overall Stan program, it's still better than having the integrator be stuck. Another workaround would be to put more into the model: better priors, better parameter declarations, etc.

For concreteness, after definig alpha_ab, you could do something like:

        if (alpha_ab > 10000)
          reject("alpha_ab is too large: ", alpha_ab);
